title: Autopsy and Letter
premise: When the coffin of Aldous Merrivale, founder of the cathedral town of Corrowick, is exhumed for a state ceremony, archivist Tamsin Yarrow discovers it empty — and a letter hidden in the crypt wall naming six heirs to a fortune no one knew existed. As Tamsin decodes the letter's cipher, the named heirs begin dying in ways that mirror deaths recorded in the cathedral's own burial ledgers, and the police detective leading the case, Inspector Rhea Vance, realizes the killer is working from a case file only someone inside the investigation could possess. Tamsin must decide whether loyalty to his mentor — the cathedral's dying dean, who helped bury the truth forty years ago — matters more than justice for the dead. In the end, Tamsin traps the killer by forging a seventh heir into the letter, luring them to the crypt, where the final confrontation reveals the killer is the 'dead' founder himself, alive and avenging the family erased from history.
about_author: Vesper Galloway is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent a decade cataloguing centuries of births, marriages, and burials before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about paper trails, buried secrets, and the people who keep both.

chapters.title: The Weight of Stone
chapters.summary: Tamsin Yarrow catalogs the cathedral crypt ahead of Aldous Merrivale's ceremonial exhumation, establishing his meticulous nature and his bond with the ailing Dean Harrow. When the coffin lid is pried open on live television, it is empty except for a folded letter. POV: Tamsin. Beat: quiet order shattered by public scandal.

chapters.title: Six Names
chapters.summary: Tamsin secretly photographs the letter before police seize it: a coded testament naming six heirs to the Merrivale estate. Inspector Rhea Vance arrives from the capital, brusque and skeptical of the archivist. Tamsin recognizes one cipher symbol from the dean's old notebooks. POV: Tamsin. Beat: curiosity curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Ledger of the Drowned
chapters.summary: Cross-referencing burial ledgers, Tamsin finds the first heir, boatman Silas Crane, died decades ago — yet Silas Crane Jr. received an anonymous summons last week. Meanwhile Vance interviews the exhumation crew and finds a guard lying about his shift. POV: alternating Tamsin and Vance. Beat: two investigations converging uneasily.

chapters.title: First Burial
chapters.summary: Silas Crane Jr. is found drowned in the flooded lower crypt, posed exactly as a 1931 ledger entry describes a Merrivale servant's death. Vance realizes the murder replicates historical records; Tamsin realizes only someone with archive access could stage it. Suspicion falls inward. POV: Tamsin. Beat: horror at intimate knowledge weaponized.

chapters.title: The Dean's Confession, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Tamsin confronts Dean Harrow, who admits he helped conceal something forty years ago but collapses before explaining. In the hospital, Harrow presses a key into Tamsin's hand and whispers 'the second grave was never opened.' POV: Tamsin. Beat: loyalty tested by half-truths.

chapters.title: Case File 40-C
chapters.summary: Vance pulls the archived 1984 investigation into a fire at Merrivale House that killed three people — including the founder's illegitimate daughter. The original file has pages missing, replaced with clean photocopies. Someone inside law enforcement tampered decades ago. POV: Vance. Beat: institutional rot exposed.

chapters.title: Second Grave
chapters.summary: Using the dean's key, Tamsin opens a sealed family plot and finds not bones but a box of documents proving Aldous Merrivale faked his own death in 1984 and vanished. The empty coffin was deliberate — a message meant to be found now. POV: Tamsin. Beat: revelation that reframes everything.

chapters.title: Heir Number Three
chapters.summary: Heir Marguerite Osei, a solicitor, hires private protection after receiving a pressed violet — the same flower in the crypt letter. Tamsin and Vance form a wary alliance, trading information off the record. POV: Vance. Beat: reluctant trust between rivals.

chapters.title: What the Fire Didn't Take
chapters.summary: Tamsin reconstructs the missing file pages from carbon copies in the diocesan records: the 1984 fire was arson, and the investigating officer falsified the report — an officer whose signature matches Vance's late father's. POV: Vance. Beat: personal devastation; her father may be complicit.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Bargain
chapters.summary: Marguerite offers Tamsin money for the original letter, revealing she's been contacted by someone calling themselves 'A.M.' who promises the full inheritance if she helps identify the other heirs. She refuses to name her contact. POV: Tamsin. Beat: greed as a window into the killer's method.

chapters.title: The Violet Killer
chapters.summary: Marguerite is found dead in her locked office, staged per another ledger entry, violets scattered. The room was locked from inside; the only camera shows no entry. Vance suspects an accomplice within her own task force. POV: Vance. Beat: paranoia tightens; the net closes inward.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Candlelight
chapters.summary: Vance quietly investigates her own team and finds the night guard's employment record forged — he appeared from nowhere eight months ago. Tamsin, meanwhile, cracks more of the cipher: the letter isn't a will, it's a confession written by the founder. POV: alternating. Beat: the hunter realizes she's been hunted alongside.

chapters.title: Harrow Wakes
chapters.summary: Dean Harrow, lucid briefly, confesses: in 1984 he helped Merrivale fake his death to escape the family being destroyed by the corrupt officer — Vance's father — who wanted the estate. The three 'fire victims' were murdered. Harrow begs Tamsin to stop Merrivale before he kills again. POV: Tamsin. Beat: grief and betrayal braided together.

chapters.title: Two Heirs Left
chapters.summary: Protective custody fails when the safe house address leaks through police channels. Heirs four and five — an elderly nun and a teenage boy — are moved to the cathedral itself, the one building the killer seems unwilling to violate. POV: Vance. Beat: sanctuary as strategy, and a trap.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Read the Letter
chapters.summary: Teenage heir Theo reveals he received the full uncoded letter weeks ago and memorized it: it names the corrupt officer and promises 'the sixth heir will judge us all.' The sixth name is smudged — deliberately. POV: Tamsin. Beat: innocence holding the deadliest clue.

chapters.title: Father's Signature
chapters.summary: Vance digs into her father's effects and finds the stolen original file pages hidden in his desk, plus letters showing he extorted Merrivale for years. Her grief turns to resolve: she will finish what her father corrupted. POV: Vance. Beat: reclaiming legacy through opposition to it.

chapters.title: Night Vigil
chapters.summary: During a storm, the cathedral loses power. The nun is found unharmed but drugged; Theo is gone. A trail of violets leads down to the crypt. Tamsin realizes the killer never needed to break the sanctity — they were invited, wearing a familiar face. POV: Tamsin. Beat: dread made physical in darkness.

chapters.title: The Sixth Name
chapters.summary: In the crypt, Tamsin finds Theo alive, guarded by the night guard — revealed as Aldous Merrivale himself, aged but unmistakable. He explains: every victim was a descendant or agent of those who murdered his family. The sixth heir, the smudged name, is the corrupt officer's child. It is Vance. POV: Merrivale. Beat: villain's tragedy fully humanized.

chapters.title: Daughter of the File
chapters.summary: Vance descends alone, having deduced the trap Tamsin set by leaking a false location. She faces Merrivale and her father's crimes at once. He offers her a choice: die as her father's heir or help him finish the ledger. She draws her weapon on him — and on herself, refusing both. POV: Vance. Beat: climax of identity and choice.

chapters.title: Autopsy
chapters.summary: Tamsin triggers the cathedral flood alarms, filling the lower crypt and forcing Merrivale to choose between killing Vance and saving Theo from rising water. He saves the boy. Subdued, Merrivale asks only that the true ledger be read aloud over his real grave. POV: Tamsin. Beat: mercy as victory; water as judgment reversed.

chapters.title: Letter, Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Merrivale awaits trial; Vance files charges posthumously against her father and the old conspiracy. At a small ceremony, Tamsin reads the founder's confession aloud in the crypt as requested, then re-buries the letter where it lay for forty years. Harrow dies peacefully that night. POV: Tamsin. Beat: mourning, accountability, quiet peace.

chapters.title: The Empty Shelf
chapters.summary: Months on, Tamsin restores the ledgers and leaves one shelf deliberately empty — reserved for the story that can't be archived. Vance visits with coffee and an unofficial cold-case file: another town, another coffin. Tamsin smiles, locks the crypt, and says yes. POV: Tamsin. Beat: renewal; partnership born from ruin.
